verdict.rationale: Babylon.js ships dedicated llms.txt files, extensive typed API docs, and community testimony praising documentation quality and strong backwards compatibility (stability helps LLM-generated code stay valid across versions). However, community evidence also notes it has notably less public content/examples than competitors like Three.js ('a lot more written about three than Babylon'), which limits training-data exposure for LLMs, and docs are client-rendered Next.js with no markdown mirrors, hurting scrapability. Missing for 10: direct evidence of LLM code-generation success rates, broader public example corpus comparable to more-documented competitors, and machine-readable doc mirrors beyond llms.txt.
